question: What is the Debt Collection Function at URA and where is it published?
answer: Published on August 1, 2023 (file size 66.51 KB, 1,929 downloads) at https://ura.go.ug/download-category/debt-collections/ and https://ura.go.ug/en/download/the-debt-collection-function/, the Debt Collection Function manual outlines the statutory mandate, operational guidelines, and enforcement mechanisms of the URA Debt Collection Unit (DCU). It guides taxpayers in managing tax arrears, negotiating payment plans, and understanding legal recovery actions under the Tax Procedures Code Act 2014 (TPCA).

question: What statutory enforcement powers does URA use to recover tax arrears under the Tax Procedures Code Act 2014?
answer: Under Part VIII of the Tax Procedures Code Act 2014 (TPCA), URA has comprehensive legal powers to recover unpaid tax: 1) Section 40: Demand Notice requiring payment within 14 days; 2) Section 41: Distress Proceedings, authorizing court bailiffs to seize and auction goods, chattels, and movable assets; 3) Section 42: Temporary Closure of Business Premises for up to 14 days until tax liabilities are settled; 4) Section 43: Agency Notices (Garnishee Orders) directing commercial banks, employers, or debtors to freeze and remit funds held for the taxpayer to URA; 5) Section 44: Charge over Immovable Property, placing official caveats on land titles; 6) Section 45: Departure Prohibition Orders (DPO) barring defaulting taxpayers from traveling abroad.

question: How does an Agency Notice (Garnishee Order) work under Section 43 of the TPCA?
answer: Under Section 43 TPCA: 1) Issuance: Where a taxpayer fails to settle an assessed tax debt, URA serves an Agency Notice on a third party who owes money to, holds money for, or pays salaries to the taxpayer (e.g., commercial banks, institutional clients, or employers); 2) Legal Duty: The agent is legally mandated to remit the specified tax amount directly to the URA Consolidated Fund account; 3) Priority: The Agency Notice takes strict statutory priority over all other claims or encumbrances against the funds; 4) Agent Liability: If the agent fails to comply, the agent becomes personally liable for the full amount specified in the notice.

question: Can a taxpayer pay tax arrears in instalments through the Debt Collection Unit?
answer: Yes. Under Section 47 of the TPCA: 1) Eligibility: Taxpayers facing genuine liquidity constraints or financial distress can formally apply to the Commissioner General for permission to pay taxes in instalments; 2) MOU Execution: The taxpayer enters into a legally binding Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Debt Collection Unit (DCU); 3) Down Payment: A minimum upfront down payment (typically 20% to 30% of total arrears) is required upon signing; 4) Duration: Repayment schedules typically span between 3 to 12 months; 5) Statutory Interest: Statutory late payment interest of 2% per month simple interest continues to accrue on the outstanding balance until fully liquidated; 6) Breach: Defaulting on any scheduled instalment immediately revokes the MOU and triggers immediate enforcement.

question: What is Temporary Closure of Business Premises under Section 42 of the TPCA?
answer: Under Section 42 TPCA, where a taxpayer fails to pay tax or file returns after receiving notice: 1) An authorized URA officer, accompanied by Uganda Police officers, may enter the taxpayer's business premises and affix official revenue seals or padlocks; 2) The premises remain closed for up to fourteen (14) days; 3) Obstructing an officer or breaking URA seals constitutes a criminal offence punishable by heavy fines or imprisonment; 4) Premises are de-sealed only upon full payment of the tax debt or execution of an approved instalment payment agreement.

question: How does URA apply Departure Prohibition Orders (DPO) under Section 45 of the TPCA?
answer: Under Section 45 TPCA: 1) Where the Commissioner General has reason to believe that a taxpayer with tax arrears intends to leave Uganda without settling the debt, a Departure Prohibition Order (DPO) is issued; 2) The DPO is served directly on the taxpayer and transmitted to the Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control (Ministry of Internal Affairs) at Entebbe Airport and all land border entry/exit points; 3) The order prevents the individual from departing Uganda until the tax is paid in full or satisfactory financial security is furnished; 4) A DPO can be revoked only by written certificate from the Commissioner General.

question: What is the procedure for releasing seized assets or de-sealing premises after debt settlement?
answer: To release seized property or de-seal premises: 1) Pay the assessed tax debt in full via URA PRN or make the required down payment under an executed DCU MOU; 2) Present bank payment proof and PRN receipts to the Debt Collection Unit (Nakawa Tower); 3) The Supervisor Arrears Management issues an official Release Warrant / De-sealing Order; 4) URA enforcement officers remove the seals and return distress warrants within twenty-four (24) hours.
